title.rendered: IT Outsourcing in Germany vs Eastern Europe: Which Option to Choose?

content.rendered:
Germany is one of the most technologically advanced countries in Europe. It is the largest economy in Europe and has a steadily growing IT market. Software development Germany is characterized by innovation and mature infrastructure. And IT outsourcing in Germany is popular because of the high-quality of services and comfortable location.

The local ICT industry is highly developed. In 2018 there were about 92.7 thousand IT companies registered here.  And there were about 1,550 startups at the same time.

20% of the revenue brought by the ICT market in Germany is generated by product innovations. For example, Germany was believed to be the largest cloud market in the EU by 2020. Germany IT nearshoring also relies heavily on security solutions. The revenue from the ICT market is expected to reach $49,205 million by 2021.

But it is not as easy to find remote specialists here as IT nearshoring for German companies is a common solution. One of the main reasons for Germany software outsourcing trend is that the country experiences a shortage of skilled professionals. Only 4.9% of higher education graduates are future ICT specialists, which is not enough for the current market.

Although many international businesses want to invest in IT outsourcing in Germany, there is a lack of workforce to fulfill the need. The spheres that are in the most demand of such SW developer are AI, IoT, and Big Data. So the employment market for IT outsourcing Germany is very competitive.

Other technologies that are in high demand for Germany nearshoring software development are:

  • Python;
  • Data Storage, Architecture, and Analysis;
  • Cyber Security;
  • CRM solutions;
  • Machine Learning;
  • DevOps.

Many German companies choose nearshoring software development in Europe or other destinations because it is simpler and more cost-efficient in terms of hiring costs and legislation.

So while many businesses look for software development companies in Germany, local businesses are also interested in delegating their tasks outside the country.

IT Outsourcing in Germany vs Eastern Europe

Luckily, software development Germany is not the only European destination out there. Nowadays, Eastern Europe is gaining momentum to fulfill the demand for remote IT services. It is popular for IT nearshoring Germany and other businesses all over the world.

The main benefits of this region are:

  • Great talent pull and high quality of services;
  • Comfortable location and time zones;
  • Decent knowledge of English;
  • Similar work ethics and business values;
  • Reasonable salaries.

Now, let’s review four main countries in Eastern Europe for IT outsourcing.

Poland

Poland is conveniently located and has several big IT hubs, such as Warsaw, Krakow, and Wroclaw. The ICT market here is developing pretty fast and is expected to produce $13 billion in revenue by 2022. The talent pool is about 295,000 developers, and the average software developer salary in the country is $2,270 per month.

The most popular technologies in Poland in 2020 were JavaScript, Java, and Python.

Bulgaria

Bulgaria has a smaller workforce than Poland, which is estimated at 24,000 experts. But it is still a great choice for many IT nearshoring Germany companies. The main IT hubs are Sofia, Varna, Plovdiv, and Burgas.  According to Clutch.co there are about 180 software development companies. And the average salary for a developer is $1,540 per month.

The IT outsourcing sector is predicted to reach 7.9% of Bulgaria’s GDP. The most popular programming languages here are JavaScript, .NET, PHP, C++, and Python.

Serbia

Another valid alternative to IT outsourcing in Germany is Serbia. The ICT sector has wide governmental support, and society moves to adopt more e-government solutions. But the use of cloud technologies is relatively low among local businesses still (35%). The ICT sector generates 10% of the country’s GDP.

There are over 2,500 companies in this industry and about 28,000 specialists. A software developer’s average salary is $1466 per month, which is cheaper than software nearshoring Germany. The main IT hubs are Belgrade, Novi Sad, Nis, Subotica, and Kragujevac.

The popular technologies here are JavaScript, .NET, PHP, Python, C#, and C++.

Estonia

Estonia is a decent competitor to Germany software nearshoring in Eastern Europe. It is one of the top 20 tech countries in the EU. It has a talent pool of 20,700 IT professionals and strong STEM education.

About 5.9% of the country’s workforce is employed in the ICT industry. Local experts are known for the quality of work, and Estonia is easy to do business in. It is also politically and economically stable. The average salary for a software developer here is $2,792 per month. And the biggest IT hubs are Tallinn and Tartu. Estonia’s popular technologies are Python, Java, PHP, VB.NET, C#, JavaScript, Android, C/C+.

Ukraine – Great Alternative to IT nearshoring Germany

Ukraine is yet another perfect destination in Eastern Europe to compete with software outsourcing Germany. It is known for cost reduction, high-quality services, and a great talent pool. The number of IT professionals here is much higher than in Estonia, Bulgaria, or Serbia. So if you are looking for a dashing alternative to Germany IT outsourcing, consider these benefits that Ukraine has to offer:

  • Comfortable location and convenient time zone (GMT+2);
  • Access to experienced professionals. There are about 200,000 IT specialists in Ukraine. Also, local universities graduate about 16,000 STEM students each year to supply the market’s demand.
  • Ukraine has similar business ethics and values, and it is pretty easy to work with local companies.
  • Ukrainian developers are known for the quality of their code. They are in 14th place worldwide, according to TopCoder.
  • Local IT professionals have a good command of English. Many of them have experience in partnering with other countries and invest in learning English. It ensures direct and easy communication.
  • Ukraine has a developed ICT infrastructure. That’s why many industry leaders and Forbes 500 companies here offices or R&D centers here, including Microsoft, Boeing, and Samsung.

Overall Attractiveness of Both Locations

The choice of outsourcing destination is based on many factors. Of course, the cost of it is essential. But the companies need to also consider other circumstances.

For example, Germany has more IT professionals than Ukraine, but it doesn’t mean that they are easier to hire. The German ICT sector is more advanced and that’s why it experiences a shortage of employees.
